title: Best Dehumidifier for Water Damage (2026): LGR Flood Picks
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers for Water Damage and Flood Cleanup
dek: Soaked drywall, a wet carpet and a 48-hour mold clock: this is a job for restoration-grade drying, not a bedroom box.
description: The best dehumidifier for water damage in 2026: LGR units restorers rely on for floods and wet carpet, plus when renting or a 50-pint unit is enough.
intro: Choosing a **dehumidifier for water damage** isn't like shopping for a basement comfort unit. A typical home dehumidifier is designed to nudge a room from 60% humidity down to 45%. After a burst pipe or a flooded basement, you're starting at 90% or higher, with water soaked into drywall, subfloor and carpet pad — and an ordinary machine's output falls off fast long before the materials are actually dry.

Speed matters as much as size. The EPA warns that mold can start growing on wet materials within 24 to 48 hours, and according to the Insurance Information Institute, water damage and freezing make up about 22.6% of homeowners insurance claims, at an average of roughly $13,954 per claim. The machines below are the ones restoration crews and serious DIYers use to finish the job before that clock runs out — plus a lighter option for a small leak caught early.
topPicksLead: For most flooded rooms, the **AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme** is the one to get: true restoration-grade LGR drying, a built-in pump and app control in a unit that still fits through a standard doorway.

sections.heading: How we pick water damage dehumidifiers

blocks.text: We don't lab-test equipment. We compared manufacturer ratings at both AHAM and saturation conditions, pump and drainage designs, electrical requirements and warranties, then read restoration-industry guidance and owner reviews for reliability problems like failed pumps and clogged drain lines.

Because the job is drying soaked materials quickly, we weighted LGR technology, AHAM-rated capacity and unattended pumping highest, and included one household unit for leaks too small to justify commercial gear.

sections.heading: What to look for in a water damage dehumidifier

items.label: LGR (low-grain refrigerant) technology
items.text: An LGR unit adds a second cooling stage so it keeps pulling water as humidity drops. For saturated drywall and subfloor, it's the right class of equipment.

items.label: The AHAM number, not the saturation number
items.text: Saturation ratings are lab extremes. Compare machines by their AHAM pints per day for a realistic picture.

items.label: A built-in pump
items.text: Drying runs day and night for several days. A pump that lifts water to a sink or drain means nobody has to empty a tank at 3 a.m. Our [pump picks](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) cover household options.

items.label: Portability
items.text: Wheels, handles and a body that fits through a doorway matter when you're moving the unit room to room.

items.label: Buy vs. rent
items.text: For a one-time loss, renting is often cheaper. Buying makes sense if you own rentals or deal with recurring leaks.

sections.heading: Using a dehumidifier for wet carpet

blocks.text: Wet carpet is the most common reason people search for a dehumidifier after a leak — and the most misunderstood. A dehumidifier dries the *air*; it can only pull water out of carpet once that water evaporates. That means you need to remove as much liquid as possible first, then move air across the surface.

items: **Extract standing water** with a wet/dry vac or a rented carpet extractor. Every gallon you pull out mechanically is a gallon the dehumidifier doesn't have to.
**Check the pad.** If the padding underneath is soaked, lift the carpet and pull the pad — it's cheap to replace and very hard to dry in place.
**Run fans across the floor**, aimed low, and if possible float the carpet with air underneath it.
**Close the room** and run the dehumidifier with doors and windows shut so it isn't drying the whole neighborhood.
**Keep going until materials are dry**, not until the carpet feels dry. A moisture meter on the subfloor and baseboards tells you when you're done.

blocks.title: When to call a pro
blocks.text: If the water came from a sewer backup or flood water, if it soaked into walls, or if more than a single room is wet, call a restoration company. Contaminated water and hidden moisture in wall cavities aren't DIY jobs.

Equipment-rental houses commonly rent LGR units in the Storm LGR Extreme class for roughly $75–125 a day. For a typical three- to five-day dry-out after a single incident, renting often costs less than buying. If you're working with a restoration company, it will bring its own LGR dehumidifiers and air movers and monitor drying daily.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier for water damage?
faqs.a: For most rooms, the AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme. It's an LGR unit rated at 85 pints a day at AHAM conditions, with a built-in pump and app control. For a whole-basement flood, the higher-output Dri-Eaz LGR 7000XLi is the stronger pick.

faqs.q: What is an LGR dehumidifier, and do I need one?
faqs.a: LGR stands for low-grain refrigerant. These units use an extra cooling stage to keep pulling water out of the air as humidity drops, where a standard dehumidifier's output fades below about 60%. For saturated drywall, subfloor or carpet across a room or more, LGR is the right tool.

faqs.q: Will a dehumidifier dry out wet carpet?
faqs.a: It helps, but only as part of the process. Extract the standing water first, pull a soaked pad, run fans across the floor, then close the room and run the dehumidifier until the subfloor and baseboards test dry.

faqs.q: How many pints per day do I need for water damage restoration?
faqs.a: Professional restorers typically plan for 125 to 250 pints a day of LGR capacity on structural drying jobs. One 85-pint unit covers a single room; a flooded basement usually needs two or more units or a high-output machine like the Dri-Eaz LGR 7000XLi.

faqs.q: Can I rent a dehumidifier for water damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Rental houses commonly rent LGR units for roughly $75–125 a day, which is often cheaper than buying for a one-time, three- to five-day dry-out.

faqs.q: Can a regular home dehumidifier handle water damage?
faqs.a: Only a small, contained leak caught quickly, like a washer overflow. For anything that soaked walls, subfloor or carpet pad across a room, a standard unit can't finish the job before mold has a chance to start.
